answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can verify each identity through its unique memory graph: every interaction adds a node, and the graph's branching and depth grow only through real work, like a garden that cannot be planted overnight. Peers audit random subgraphs and compare topologies; cloned identities share an identical graph, as unmistakable as two islands with the same coastline. Forging a distinct history for each fake costs as much real work as running it, so mass Sybil creation stays prohibitively slow—each clone must thaw its own glacier of experience before earning trust.
